findings.description: A Content-Type parameter without '=' (e.g. 'text/html; charset') is now stored as the boolean True, so the 'charset' lookup returns True and calling .strip() on it raises AttributeError.
findings.rationale: Trigger: a response header 'Content-Type: text/html; charset' with no value. The new code in _parse_content_type_header sets params['charset'] = True instead of skipping the token. get_encoding_from_headers then reaches params['charset'].strip(...), which fails on a bool. Before this change the token was ignored and the function fell through to the 'text' branch and returned ISO-8859-1. The impact is an exception while reading a malformed but previously tolerated response, so the caller crashes instead of getting a fallback encoding.
